scenes.text: Imagine standing in the absolute middle of the Sahara Desert, where for two hundred and fifty miles in every single direction, there is absolutely nothing but sand except for one single, heroic acacia tree.
Known as the Tree of Ténéré, it was the most isolated tree on Earth, acting as a sacred landmark for desert travelers for decades with roots digging over a hundred feet deep just to find water.

But in nineteen seventy-three, the unthinkable happened when a truck driver, allegedly drunk and following a flat, open road with infinite space, somehow drove directly into this one solitary tree, knocking it down.
It survived centuries of harsh desert heat only to be taken out by human stupidity, so would you have managed to miss it, let me know in the comments and subscribe for more mind-blowing history.

meta.title: The only tree for 250 miles was hit by a drunk driver #shorts
